messages:
anya: quick triage — after the kernel-selector tweak landed yesterday (auto-fp16 fallback change) we're seeing host-side p50 increase from ~7ms -> ~12ms for seq<=64 workloads. flamegraph: https://internal/fg/61333377 — looks like tokenization and request.parse_path jumped.

sam: saw this in perf dashboard too. p95 up as well? any correlation with KV cache hits?

anya: p95 up from 45ms -> 82ms on same tests. KV cache hit rate steady. stack from perf: parse_request 38%, token_streamer::emit 22%, grpc_writev 14%, sys_write 8%.

mike: grpc_writev at 14% is suspicious — we've got smallwrite churn. Did the selector change affect batching? could be different batching threshold causing more host-side write syscalls.

lee: can you paste the flame snippet? also what's batching config? default max_batch_tokens=2048? and host_autobatch_threshold was 24 -> 16 in the patch?

anya: flame snippet:
```
parse_request
  token_streamer::emit
    grpc_writev
      sys_write
```
batching config: host_autobatch_threshold=16 (from last change). kernel selector change only touched device kernels, but we also added a short-seq fastpath that avoids large kernel but forces more host framing.

sam: hypothesis: faster kernels for certain seqs caused earlier returns to host, increasing small writes and parse churn. more context switches + writev -> higher p50.

mike: quick repro: run microbench with seq=32, rate 2000 qps, --use-kernel=auto vs --use-kernel=legacy. I can run later.

lee: experiment suggestion: revert host_autobatch_threshold -> 24 and re-run to see if amortizes write overhead. Also try enabling prefix KV caching offload (kv_prefetch=false) to check parse hotspots.

anya: I ran threshold=24 locally, p50 dropped to ~8ms. p95 still 60ms. With kv_prefetch=false negligible change.

sam: good signal. Next steps: (1) canary revert threshold to 24 on canary pool; (2) instrument tracepoints around grpc_writev to capture writev batch sizes; (3) add microbench into CI for seq<=64 to catch regressions.

deploy-bot: canary started on pool 'canary-12' by @anya

mike: I'll add a perf-counter to count writev ops per request and distribute a quick patch. also let's consider coalescing small frames at host preparse layer — we do a token-emit per chunk currently.

lee: low-risk coalesce patch: buffer up to 256 bytes or until EOS then one writev. I'll prototype.

anya: assign @lee and @mike. thanks. anyone object to reverting threshold on canary? :+1:

sam: +1

mike: +1

lee: starting prototyping now, will push wip branch and shortbench results in thread.

perf-bot: perf alert cleared for canary pool after revert

anya: closing loop — thanks team. we'll monitor for 24h and follow up with root-cause writeup.
